1: # Architecture overview
     2: 
     3: wg-basic is a Linux-native WireGuard management appliance: one small Rust
     4: executable with two separated privilege domains. The Linux kernel owns the
     5: WireGuard dataplane. This document is the bird's-eye view and the index for
     6: the per-component deep dives in this directory. Those files describe
     7: **current implemented behavior**; planned work belongs in `plans/`.
     8: 
     9: ## Bird's-eye view
    10: 
    11: ```text
    12: operator / browser
    13:       │  HTTPS via reverse proxy, or loopback HTTP
    14:       ▼
    15: serve (unprivileged management role) ── owns ──► SQLite state store (authoritative)
    16:   │  embedded EggServe HTTP surface          monotonic desired generation + CAS
    17:   │  one bounded worker thread holds         installation identity, owner tags,
    18:   │  ManagementRuntime; HTTP code never      convergence evidence, credentials,
    19:   │  touches the store or netd directly      product metadata, audit history
    20:   │                                              │
    21:   │  typed request over local UDS socket         │  one aggregate intent per
    22:   │  (SO_PEERCRED authorized, no shell,          │  generation, projected from
    23:   │   no raw netlink/nft/sysctl/file ops)       │  the committed snapshot
    24:   ▼                                              ▼
    25: netd (privileged network role, CAP_NET_ADMIN) ◄── ManagementRuntime::reconcile
    26:   │  typed WireGuard observation/patch (Generic Netlink, nl-wireguard)
    27:   │  typed link/address/route reconcile (RTNETLINK, rtnetlink)
    28:   │  typed IPv4 forwarding/NAT/firewall policy (bounded nft subprocess)
    29:   │  ownership proven per resource (IFLA_IFALIAS tags, table markers)
    30:   └──► kernel state (derivative — only ever observed, never authoritative)
    31: ```
    32: 
    33: Two invariants shape everything:
    34: 
    35: - **State authority.** SQLite desired state is authoritative; kernel state is
    36:   derivative. Startup reconciles unconditionally because the kernel may have
    37:   drifted while stopped. A late receipt can never mark a newer generation
    38:   converged.
    39: - **Privilege separation.** Only the unprivileged management role opens the
    40:   database (`netd` is database-free). Only `netd` touches the kernel, and only
    41:   through typed operations. There is no arbitrary shell, command, file-write,
    42:   sysctl-path, nft-script, or raw-netlink execution anywhere in the protocol.
    43: 
    44: ## Discrete modules and where to dive deeper
    45: 
    46: | Source subtree | Owns | Deep dive |
    47: |---|---|---|
    48: | `src/domain/` | typed identifiers, interface-name validation, IP prefix values, key/secret wrappers, generation, owner tags, intent/state shells | [domain-model](domain-model.md) |
    49: | `src/state/` | hardened SQLite store, ordered migrations, installation identity, CAS generations, projection, convergence evidence, backup/restore, service/maintenance leases | [state-store](state-store.md) |
    50: | `src/protocol/` | versioned UDS protocol: framing, peer-credential auth, capability inspection, dispatch, typed client | [privilege-boundary](privilege-boundary.md) |
    51: | `src/wireguard/` | kernel WireGuard backend over Generic Netlink (device/peer observe/patch, telemetry) | [wireguard-control](wireguard-control.md) |
    52: | `src/firewall/` | typed IPv4 forwarding/NAT policy, planner, bounded `nft` service, owned-table model | [firewall](firewall.md) |
    53: | `src/reconcile/` + `src/aggregate.rs` | deterministic link/address/route planner, Linux applier, aggregate coordinator, receipts | [reconciliation](reconciliation.md) |
    54: | ownership markers | `IFLA_IFALIAS` owner tags, `inet wg_basic` table markers, aggregate generation monotonicity, fail-closed rules | [ownership](ownership.md) |
    55: | `src/management/` | runtime lifecycle, bounded worker, reconcile coordinator, health projection, credential/session operations | [startup-recovery](startup-recovery.md), [management-http](management-http.md), [authentication](authentication.md) |
    56: | `src/http/` | EggServe surface: routing, Host/Origin/CSRF perimeter, security headers, rate limits, readiness, embedded assets, `serve` lifecycle | [management-http](management-http.md) |
    57: | `src/management/auth.rs` + `src/domain/auth.rs` | Argon2id credentials, opaque digest-only sessions, cookie/CSRF profile, login/logout/session routes | [authentication](authentication.md) |
    58: | `src/product/` | server setup, client lifecycle, address allocation, config/QR export, one-time enrollment, telemetry, audit, embedded product UI | [product-management](product-management.md) |
    59: | `src/distribution.rs` | canonical system layout, authenticated metadata identity, exact systemd/sysusers material, local install/status transaction | [service-hardening](service-hardening.md) |
    60: | `src/doctor.rs` + `src/operational.rs` + maintenance | read-only doctor/preflight, structured stderr events, service/maintenance leases, disable/enable/purge, backup/restore ops | [diagnostics-maintenance](diagnostics-maintenance.md) |
    61: | `src/main.rs` CLI roles | `serve`, `netd`, `reconcile`, `health`, `doctor`, `admin`, `state`, `network`, `system install/status` command surface | [cli-roles](cli-roles.md) |
    62: | `tests/` + fixtures | unprivileged suites, rootful namespace fixtures, static architecture guards, upgrade rehearsal | [testing-qualification](testing-qualification.md) |
    63: | service contract | product-owned systemd service definitions and hardening profile | [service-hardening](service-hardening.md) |
    64: | update contract | current M004 transaction implementation, binary+database rollback order, crash-window matrix, and qualification status | [update-rollback-contract](update-rollback-contract.md) |
    65: 
    66: ## Tools and capabilities (operator view)
    67: 
    68: - **Serve the appliance:** `wg-basic serve` (unprivileged HTTP + worker),
    69:   `wg-basic netd` (privileged UDS backend). Loopback by default; routable binds
    70:   and HTTPS origins are explicit, acknowledged deployments. See
    71:   [cli-roles](cli-roles.md) and [management-http](management-http.md).
    72: - **Administer credentials:** `wg-basic admin set-password --password-stdin`
    73:   (stdin only, never argv/env), `wg-basic admin status` (safe projection).
    74:   See [authentication](authentication.md).
    75: - **Inspect and recover state:** `state status|backup|restore|verify`,
    76:   `network status|disable|enable`, `state purge` (guarded, needs
    77:   disabled+converged+no-op plan), `health`, `doctor` (read-only,
    78:   exit 0/1/2). See [cli-roles](cli-roles.md) and
    79:   [diagnostics-maintenance](diagnostics-maintenance.md).
    80: - **Run the product:** login/session/health, one-time server setup, managed
    81:   client CRUD with `expected_generation` compare-and-swap (`200`/`201`
    82:   enforced vs `202` pending), explicit config/QR export, one-time enrollment
    83:   links, live telemetry, bounded audit pages, embedded UI. See
    84:   [product-management](product-management.md).
    85: - **Qualify a change:** ordinary `cargo test`, rootful namespace suites with
    86:   `--features linux-integration`, static guards in
    87:   `tests/architecture_guards.rs`. See
    88:   [testing-qualification](testing-qualification.md) and
    89:   [development](../docs/development.md).
    90: 
    91: ## Status
    92: 
    93: Network control, durable state/restart reconciliation (Phases 6),
    94: management/auth substrate (Phase 7), product/enrollment/UI (Phase 8), and
    95: operational hardening (Phase 9) are closed. Phase 10 M001–M004 technical
    96: implementation and qualification are closed, including signed-fixture
    97: systemd update, rollback, interruption recovery, and native x86_64/aarch64
    98: release artifacts. Phase 10 lifecycle qualification is closed, including
    99: native systemd install/uninstall/reinstall evidence on both supported targets.
   100: Production updates remain unavailable until a maintainer-provisioned trust
   101: root and signed release are available; technical Phase 10 closure does not
   102: authorize publication.
   103: Implementation status lives in
   104: [the planning registry](../plans/registry.md).
